rationale: ary3 is a tiny (512-byte text, essentially one hot loop in main) runtime-bound numeric kernel from the Shootout suite, so cost dimensions act as strong gates: FLA and BCF get very high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights because flattening and bogus-path cloning multiply the iteration cost of the dominant loop and bloat a 512-byte binary while yielding little security on a straight-line, low-branch-count kernel; IBR keeps decent Security/Diversity weights (loop back-edges and the main conditional are the only real control-flow surface worth disguising) but a high RuntimeCost gate to keep indirect-branch overhead out of the hot path; SUB is the best fit here — the kernel is arithmetic-heavy and substitution adds moderate diversity at low runtime and correctness cost, so its cost gates are relaxed; SPLIT is cheap and low-risk and helps fragment the modest control-flow graph; ICALL and IGV are held at low-moderate weights since the profile shows almost no indirect calls or global-variable traffic to obfuscate, making their diversity contribution marginal while CorrectnessRisk gates are kept to protect the single hot function.
